GOAL: pick a curvature-coupling position not yet measured, after three curvature arms failed on layer-3 collapse (holonomy-path-behaviour-rq: l2_distinct_prefixes=1, l3_collision=1.0; GEOCAP-RQ: l1_hard_er 3.885, hit_rate 0.1222, l2 4236, l3_collision 0.549, refinement 2.82b, rejected by 35% gate; OCCURV-FIELD-RQ: l1_hard_er 2.488, hit_rate 0.2629, l2 784, l3_collision 0.943, 2.32b, rejected).
READ: no workspace files available to this session (no write/no shell); decided from the round diagnosis only.
OBSERVED/REASONED: first-order separation comes from curvature in the assignment metric; layer-3 collapse comes from the same curvature squeezing codewords where residuals are small. So the mechanism must (a) make curvature literally per-layer and decaying to ~Euclidean at depth, and (b) add an independent spreading force at depth that is behavioural, not geometric. Unused position in the design space: entropic optimal-transport / Sinkhorn assignment whose cost is a per-layer geodesic distance plus a Karcher-mean behaviour target, with a column-uniform marginal that guarantees codeword spread. That is neither holonomy (no path transport), nor GEOCAP (no per-codeword radii from popularity), nor OCCURV-FIELD (no per-codeword curvature field; one curvature per layer).
OPEN: derived (not tuned) formulas for a_l, kappa_l, epsilon_l and the successor-code cache.
ANSWER (full block):
IDEA: strataot-curv-rq
TITLE: Stratified-curvature, behaviour-marginal hyperbolic Sinkhorn assignment for RQ-VAE Semantic IDs
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE SIDs are assigned by nearest-codeword under a flat metric, so an item and its habitual successors can land in unrelated prefixes and the deepest level saturates on a few codewords, which caps Stage3 next-item recall. Curvature fixed level-1 separation but crushed level 3 because deep residuals are small and sit where the curved metric is most distorting.
NOVELTY: None of the three prior curvature arms used a transport plan. Here the assignment itself is a doubly-stochastic entropic OT plan: the ground cost is a per-layer geodesic distance (curvature radius tied to the layer's remaining residual mass, so curvature literally decays with depth and level 3 is almost flat), the cost carries a second term to the Karcher mean of the item's training successor codewords (per-pair behaviour), the column marginal is uniform (the explicit deep-layer spreading force), and the straight-through path is the plan itself. No transport along paths (holonomy), no popularity radii (GEOCAP), no per-codeword curvature field (OCCURV).
CHANGE: The RQ assignment of layer l becomes argmax of a Sinkhorn plan on a curvature-normalised geodesic cost matrix that is augmented with the geodesic distance from each codeword to the hyperbolic centroid of the item's training-successor codewords; the reconstruction keeps the hard codeword in the forward pass and takes its encoder/codebook gradient through the plan.
SPECIFICATION: see SPEC EQUATIONS / SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS below; three switches USE_BEHAVIOUR (successor term + behaviour target in the cost), USE_HYPERBOLIC (kappa_l curved distances, exp/log/Karcher instead of identity/arithmetic mean) and both-on exist in code; only both-on is trained.
COST: Stage 2 only; per step (B~1024 residuals, K codewords, L=3, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72k steps) adds 3*B*K geodesic terms (~0.8M at K=256, ~3.1M at K=1024) plus 16 log-domain Sinkhorn sweeps on 3 matrices B x K, i.e. roughly +10 to +18 percent step time and

a few MB of activation memory; the successor table is 24556 x 3 bytes and the Karcher step is 3 iterations on 8 neighbours per item.
HYPOTHESIS: If the collapse is caused by curvature at depth rather than by the RQ residual itself, then decaying kappa_l with remaining residual mass plus a balanced transport marginal must keep valid_l1_hard_er <= 4 and positive_hit_rate >= 0.12 while pushing l3_collision under 0.35, level2_distinct_prefixes above 4000 and refinement near 2.8 bits, which is the configuration that can move Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, best 0.0638).
RISKS: RQ residual mass may not decay enough for kappa_l to separate the layers, so level 3 would stay curved and collapse again; the epoch-lagged successor code table can oscillate; column-uniform balancing can fight item identity and raise level-1 hard ER; items with no training successor fall back to a pure geodesic cost and dilute the behaviour term; per-layer percentiles add noise at the start of training while the residual scale is still moving.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions (sequential co-consumption), used per item-successor pair as integer weights w_ij, plus the previous-epoch hard codeword of each successor.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: for each item i, count directed transitions i->j inside the training sequences, keep the top M=8 successors by count as Succ(i) with weights w_ij (counts). Once per epoch, store each training item's hard codeword at each layer T_l[i] from the forward pass of that epoch; the next epoch uses the previous table. Both are pure training-split statistics.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The successor lists, successor weights and the codeword table T_l are built exclusively from training-split sequences and from encoder forward passes on training batches; validation/test interactions are never read, never cached and never used in the codebook, the curvature statistics or the transport marginals. The curvature radii use only training residuals.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare-ball geodesic distance with trainable-free per-layer negative curvature kappa_l = -1/a_l^2, its exponential map exp_0 (residual into the ball) and logarithmic map log_p (for the Karcher mean); a_l = q_l * S_1/S_l is derived from measured residual scales, so |kappa_l| decreases with depth and layer 3 is nearly Euclidean while still evaluated through the curved map.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the layer-l RQ quantisation step (assignment cost, behaviour target and reconstruction), for every one of the L=3 residual levels, with the same curvature and the same codeword positions used for assignment and reconstruction.
COUPLING PATH: One cost matrix per layer, C_ic = d_(kappa_l)(u_i, e_c)^2 / a_l^2 + d_(kappa_l)(e_c, b_i^l)^2 / a_l^2 with b_i^l the Karcher mean of the successor codewords, is fed to a Sinkhorn plan whose argmax assigns the code and whose soft version carries the gradient; removing the behaviour term changes b_i and the cost, removing curvature changes the distances, the exp/log maps, the Karcher mean and the layer schedule, so neither switch leaves the computation intact.
COUPLING EQUATION: C_ic = [ d_(kappa_l)(exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_i^l), e_c) ]^2 / a_l^2 + [ d_(kappa_l)(e_c, Frechet_{kappa_l}({e_{T_l[j]}} : j in Succ(i), w_ij)) ]^2 / a_l^2, P = Sinkhorn(C / eps_l, rows 1/B, cols 1/K), c_i = argmax_c P_ic, z_i^l = e_{c_i} + (sum_c P_ic e_c - sg(sum_c P_ic e_c)).
OBSERVABLES: valid_l1_hard_er (expect <= 4), positive_hit_rat

e (expect >= 0.12), level2_distinct_prefixes (expect > 4000), l3_collision (expect <= 0.35), refinement bits (expect ~2.8), per-layer codeword usage entropy (expect flat across layers instead of collapsing at level 3), and Stage3 test_recall@10 as the only judgement.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: USE_BEHAVIOUR=False: b_i term deleted, cost = d_(kappa_l)(...) / a_l only, and no successor table is read; geometry and Sinkhorn unchanged. Exists in code, not trained.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: USE_HYPERBOLIC=False: kappa_l = 0, exp/log become identity, d becomes Euclidean ||.||/a_l, the Karcher mean becomes the weighted arithmetic mean, and d^2 is used in the same Sinkhorn; behaviour term unchanged. Exists in code, not trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The single trained candidate: per-layer decaying kappa_l, geodesic cost plus Karcher-mean behaviour term, Sinkhorn with uniform column marginal and plan-based straight-through.
SPEC EQUATIONS: (1) per epoch measure q_l = 90th percentile of ||r_i^l|| and S_l = mean_i sum_{m>=l} ||r_i^m|| over the epoch's training batches; set a_l = q_l * S_1 / S_l, kappa_l = -1/a_l^2. (2) p = exp_0^{kappa}(v) = tanh(sqrt(|kappa|)||v||/2) * v / (sqrt(|kappa|)||v||), with 0 handled by a Taylor branch. (3) d_(kappa)(p,q) = 2/sqrt(|kappa|) * artanh( sqrt(|kappa|) * ||(-p) xor q|| / sqrt((1-|kappa||p|^2)(1-|kappa||q|^2)) ), then divide by a_l. (4) b_i = Karcher: p <- e_{T[j*]}, j* = most frequent successor; repeat 3 times: p <- exp_p( sum_j w_ij log_p(e_{T[j]}) / sum_j w_ij ). (5) C_ic as in COUPLING EQUATION; eps_l = mean_i min_c C_ic (measured per step), floored at 1e-8. (6) 16 log-domain Sinkhorn iterations with marginals 1/B and 1/K. (7) c_i = argmax_c P_ic (lowest index on ties); z_i^l = e_{c_i} + (sum_c P_ic e_c - sg(sum_c P_ic e_c)); r_i^{l+1} = r_i^l - z_i^l. (8) Losses unchanged from the baseline RQ-VAE (reconstruction + commitment); no new loss term is introduced.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: layer-l residual matrix R (B x d) from the frozen encoder/previous levels, codebook E_l (K x d), the training-split successor lists with weights, the previous-epoch codeword table T_l, the previous-epoch scalars q_l and S_l. Outputs: hard code indices c_i, quantised vector z_i^l (forward value equal to e_{c_i}), next residual r_i^{l+1}, the plan P (detached after use), and refreshed q_l, S_l and T_l at epoch end.
SAFEGUARDS: log-domain Sinkhorn with clamping of the cost at 1e3 * eps_l to avoid inf; eps_l floored at 1e-8 and rescaled if a row has all-equal costs; exp_0 Taylor branch for ||v|| < 1e-6; artanh argument clamped to 1 - 1e-7; a_l floored at 1e-3 and kappa_l capped at 1e-4 in magnitude so the nearly-Euclidean deep layer never divides by zero; q_l replaced by the running value when an epoch has fewer than 100 residuals at that layer; uniform fallback for items with empty Succ(i) (behaviour term dropped for that row); successor table refreshed only at epoch boundaries so it cannot chase itself within an epoch; the codeword table and successor lists are detached from the graph and never receive gradient.
END IDEA
